9.	X’s father was a prosperous owner of copper mines and smelters. He was determined to see X, his eldest son, become a lawyer. Later in life, X compared his education to purgatory and hell. After a terrifying experience in a thunderstorm, he abandoned his legal studies and became an Augustinian friar. Tormented by the question of how a sinful person could be justified before God, he developed the doctrine of "sola fide" — salvation by faith alone. When summoned before the Diet of Worms and asked to recant his heretical beliefs, he declared: “here I stand, I can do no other.” ID X.
